memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: But the woman had taken the two men and hidden them. She said, "Yes, the men came to me, but I did not know where they had come from. At dusk, when it was time to close the city gate, they left. I don't know which way they went. Go after them quickly. You may catch up with them." — Josh 2:4-5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Rahab makes her choice: she hides the spies and sends the king's men on a wild goose chase. Many readers pause here, and rightly so. Rahab told a lie. Does the Bible approve of lying?

We must be honest with the text rather than tidy it up. Scripture records Rahab's deception without directly praising the lie itself. What the New Testament commends is her faith — that she "welcomed the spies" and acted to protect God's people (Heb 11:31; Jas 2:25). Rahab was a new believer, freshly turning from a pagan city, with everything to learn. God met her where she was, in her weakness, and honoured the faith behind her action even though her methods were imperfect.

That is deeply encouraging for us. God does not wait for us to become flawless before He begins to work in us. He takes hold of imperfect people and grows them. Rahab's faith was real even while her understanding was still small.

None of this makes lying good. Rather, it shows a God of grace who looks at the heart turning toward Him. That same grace meets us in Christ, who receives sinners as they are and then patiently makes them new (Rom 5:8).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you waiting to "clean yourself up" before coming to God, instead of coming as you are?
2. How does it comfort you that God honoured Rahab's faith while she was still learning?
3. Where is God patiently growing you beyond your old ways?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You receive me in my weakness and grow me over time. Take my imperfect faith and make it strong and true. Amen.
